items.text: Will start Wednesday. Caruso will start Wednesday's preseason game against the Rockets, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports. Caruso didn't start Monday's preseason opener against the Spurs. However, the Thunder had an unusual starting lineup that night due to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Luguentz Dort resting. Caruso will be joined in the first five Wednesday by Gilgeous-Alexander, Dort, Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren, with Isaiah Hartenstein notably coming off the bench again.
Not part of starting linuep. Caruso won't start Monday's preseason game against the Spurs, Rylan Stiles of FanSided.com reports. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Likely extension candidate. Caruso is expected to get a contract extension from the Thunder once he becomes eligible in December, Rylan Stiles of SI.com reports. The guard was acquired from the Bulls over the summer in exchange for Josh Giddey, and Caruso's defensive acumen should be a good fit on the OKC roster. "I think it's clear that he fits a lot of the characteristics and the criteria that we value," Thunder GM Sam Presti said Wednesday. "We know, I think, enough to want to have him here for a really long time based on his performance at his different stops." Caruso averaged a career-high 10.1 points, 1.9 three-pointers and 1.7 steals per game last season for Chicago over 71 regular-season contests.

Won't play in SL finale. The Wizards ruled Sarr out for Saturday's Summer League game against the Bucks. It doesn't appear that Sarr is dealing with an injury considering he is one of seven prominent players taking a seat for Washington's final Summer League contest. The No. 2 overall pick struggled on the offensive end in Vegas but flashed the rim protection and defensive versatility that makes him such an intriguing prospect at seven feet tall.

Shooting woes continue Thursday. Sarr finished just 1-of-6 from the floor for two points over 28 minutes, adding 11 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in an exhibition win over the Kings on Thursday. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Lackluster performance Sunday. Sarr recorded eight points (4-14 FG, 0-5 3Pt), four rebounds, two assists and two blocks across 29 minutes during Sunday's Summer League game against the Rockets. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Game-high four blocks in win Friday. Sarr tallied 12 points (4-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, four assists, four blocks and one steal across 32 minutes in Friday's 94-88 win over the Hawks in the NBA 2K25 Summer League. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Praised by Wizards' general manager. Wizards general manager Will Dawkins praised Sarr on Tuesday and said fans should be excited about what he might be able to accomplish in his rookie season. "I wouldn't put limitations on it, to be honest with you," Dawkins said about Sarr during an appearance on a Monumental Sports Network podcast. "He'll have his moments throughout the beginning of the year, both negative and positive. But the stuff he can do on the floor long-term, I think you guys will be pretty excited about." Sarr was selected with the second overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, and even though the big man struggled in the 2024 Summer League, he might be ready to make an impact right out of the gate on a rebuilding Wizards team. It's unclear if he'll play at power forward or center in a long-term scenario, but the Wizards will give Sarr all the playing time he can handle to see what they have in the promising big man.

Will lead backcourt in 2024-25. Simons is expected to open the 2024-25 season as a regular starter, according to Sean Highkin of Rose Garden Report. This isn't exactly a surprise, as Simons is one of the cornerstones of the Trail Blazers' rebuilding process, but it means Scoot Henderson, who was drafted with the second overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, will likely come off the bench. Expect Simons to operate as Portland's go-to player on offense after he delivered career-high averages of 22.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 3.4 triples across 34.4 minutes per game in 46 starts during the 2023-24 campaign.

Starting against South Sudan. Davis is starting Wednesday's Olympic matchup against South Sudan. Davis dealt with an illness ahead of the Olympics but was still able to suit up in Sunday's matchup against Serbia as the United States began Olympic play. He tallied seven points (3-6 FG, 1-1 FT), eight rebounds, an assist and a steal in 19 minutes off the bench during the 110-84 win over Serbia and will replace Joel Embiid in Wednesday's starting lineup.

Expected to play Sunday. Coach Steve Kerr said Saturday that he expects Davis (illness) to play in Sunday's Olympic matchup versus Serbia, BasketNews.com reports. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Keen on finding frontcourt partner. Davis wants to play alongside another big man more often in the 2024-25 season, according to Dave McMenamin of ESPN. Davis has made clear to the Lakers that he wants to play alongside another big man more often, and it seems this also indicates he wants to play as a power forward rather than as a center. However, with Christian Wood injured to begin the season, Jaxson Hayes and Colin Castleton are the only healthy true bigs on the roster. The Lakers also signed Christian Koloko, who could be an option to add depth in the frontcourt.

Stellar outing in Olympic win. Edwards totaled 26 points (11-15 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-4 FT), three rebounds, three assists and two steals across 17 minutes in Team USA's 104-83 win over Puerto Rico in the Paris Olympics on Saturday. Edwards was firing on all cylinders in the blowout win, and he also became the youngest player since Dwight Howard in 2008 to score 20-plus points for Team USA in the Olympics. The young star has been a top option for Team USA in the group phase, and he will likely continue to serve as a top contributor off the bench in the Olympic quarterfinals. Edwards averaged 16.7 points and 3.0 rebounds across 17.7 minutes per game in three group-stage appearances.

Scores in double figures off bench. Edwards posted 13 points (4-9 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three steals, two assists and one rebound in 17 minutes during Team USA's 103-86 win over South Sudan on Wednesday. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Out for Summer League. Thompson won't participate in Summer League while recovering from a blood clot, James L. Edwards III of The Athletic reports. Thompson's rookie season was cut short in March after undergoing treatment for a blood clot. He finished with averages of 8.8 points, 6.4 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals across 25.1 minutes in 63 regular-season games. The Pistons are likely playing it safe with the 21-year-old, as he is expected to ramp up on-court activity during the summer and be ready for training camp in the fall.

Could secure starting role. Thompson could open the 2024-25 season as part of the Pistons' starting lineup, James Edwards III of The Athletic speculates. Edwards believes Thompson could find his way into the starting lineup to add much-needed balance to the backcourt, as his defensive ability and versatility could play well alongside Cade Cunningham. The Pistons are surprisingly strong in terms of depth at the shooting guard position, which would also allow them to use Malik Beasley as part of an improved second unit alongside Tim Hardaway and Jaden Ivey.

Efficient off bench. Adebayo recorded 18 points (8-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt), seven rebounds, two blocks, one assist and one steal in 21 minutes during Team USA's 103-86 win over South Sudan on Wednesday. Adebayo didn't see much volume during Sunday's win over Serbia, but he was much more efficient during Wednesday's matchup despite coming off the bench once again. His impact could regress if Joel Embiid returns to the team's rotation, but it was encouraging to see him lead the club in scoring while tying for team-high marks in rebounds and blocks during Wednesday's matchup.

Good to go for training camp. Simmons (back) will participate in the Nets' training camp beginning Oct. 1 without any restrictions, Chris Haynes of Turner Sports reports. Simmons underwent a microscopic partial discectomy to alleviate nerve impingement in his lower back in March but appears to have made a full recovery. The 28-year-old guard made just 15 appearances, including 12 starts, for Brooklyn in 2023-24, averaging 6.1 points, 7.9 rebounds and 5.7 assists in 23.9 minutes. While injuries will always be a concern for Simmons, he could be heavily featured for a rebuilding Nets team in 2024-25.

Ready for training camp?. Simmons is recovering from a back injury but is expected to be ready for training camp, according to Brian Lewis of The New York Post. After playing just 15 games last season and undergoing back surgery in March, Simmons has been cleared for 5-on-5 and should be ready for training camp. Simmons is playing on an expiring contract, and his performances in the upcoming season will be pivotal to determining his future in the NBA. He can put up numbers when healthy, but he hasn't played more than 60 games since 2018.

Set for steady minutes. Dosunmu is considered to be a "lock" to see steady minutes off the bench for the Bulls in 2024-25, according to K.C. Johnson of NBC Sports Chicago. Johnson believes a lineup of Josh Giddey, Coby White, Zach LaVine, Patrick Williams and Nikola Vucevic is the "most logical" outcome for the starting five, but Dosunmu should see steady minutes off the bench at both guard spots. His three-point shooting and solid defensive skills are very valuable for the Bulls, so he's going to have a role one way or another. Dosunmu averaged a career-high 12.2 points per game in 76 regular-season appearances in 2023-24 while adding 2.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 0.9 steals per contest.

Extension looking unclear. The recent contract extension the Pacers gave to T.J. McConnell in the offseason could impact the team's chances of re-signing Mathurin next summer, according to Dustin Dopirak of the Indianapolis Star. The Pacers recently signed McConnell to a four-year, $45 million extension and extended Andrew Nembhard with a three-year, $58.6 million contract. This means the team is closer to the luxury tax threshold and the prohibitive tax aprons going forward, which could be a problem for small-market teams. The Pacers will eventually have to decide which players to keep around for the long haul, and Mathurin's recent injury issues could conspire against him. The second-year forward missed most of the 2023-24 campaign due to a shoulder injury, so the upcoming 2024-25 season will be pivotal for his future with the Pacers.

Efficient in Olympic win. Bogdanovic contributed 16 points (6-12 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three assists, two rebounds and one steal across 25 minutes for the Serbian national team Saturday in a 93-83 win over Serbia in the bronze medal game of the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris. The 31-year-old's perimeter shooting was crucial for Serbia during its Olympic run, with Bogdanovic operating as the squad's No. 2 option behind Nuggets star Nikola Jokic. In six Olympic contests, Bogdanovic averaged 18.3 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.8 assists while shooting 46.2 percent from beyond the arc. He's projected to serve as a starter on the wing or as a sixth man for Atlanta during the upcoming NBA campaign.

Leads team in scoring in loss. Bogdanovic gathered 20 points (8-18 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 1-1 FT), four rebounds and three assists in 31 minutes during Thursday's 95-91 semifinal loss to the United States. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Game-high 30 points in Olympic win. Bogdanovic tallied 30 points (10-14 FG, 6-9 3Pt, 4-5 FT), eight assists, four rebounds, two blocks and two steals across 32 minutes in Serbia's 96-85 win over South Sudan in the Paris Olympics on Saturday. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Scores 14 points in Olympic loss. Bogdanovic put up 14 points (6-14 FG, 2-6 3Pt), six rebounds, one assist and one steal across 28 minutes in Serbia's 110-84 loss to the United States in the Paris Olympics on Sunday. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Could earn starting role in 2024-25. Bogdanovic is expected to compete for a starting role in the Hawks' backcourt in the 2024-325 season, Lauren Williams of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution speculates. Bogdanovic seems like the most logical option to start alongside Trae Young due to his shooting ability. However, a pairing of Young and Bogdanovic could create some problems on the defensive end even though Bogdanovic has improved on that end of the floor of late. Bogdanovic averaged 17.1 points per regular-season game as a starter in 2023-24.

Cleared to play in exhibition. Bogdanovic (wrist/foot) is scheduled to play in an exhibition game Sept. 5 in Zagreb, Croatia, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports. The exhibition game is in honor of the late Drazen Petrovic, a Yugoslav and Croatian basketball legend who blazed the trail for many European players -- including Bogdanovic -- to make the jump to the NBA. Acquired from the Knicks earlier this summer in the deal that sent Mikal Bridges to New York, Bogdanovic saw his 2023-24 season come to an end in late April during the playoffs, when he sustained a left foot injury that required surgery followed by a three-month evaluation timeline. He also underwent an additional surgery on his left wrist May 22 that required a 6-to-8-week recovery, but Bogdanovic's ability to compete in the exhibition suggests that he received full medical clearance at some point in late July or early August. Bogdanovic should thus be on track to be a full participant when the Nets open training camp Oct. 1.

Starting in undersized unit. Coach Mike Budenholzer said Friday that Beal will start alongside Tyus Jones and Devin Booker in 2024-25, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports. Beal will once again be a part of a three-guard lineup in Phoenix, as Jones will replace Grayson Allen as a starter. Beal's 18.2 points per contest in 2023-24 was his lowest mark since 2015-16, but the introduction of a true point guard into the starting unit could help him return to his previous scoring form. However, the 31-year-old will still certainly be behind Kevin Durant and Devin Booker in the offensive pecking order.

Could battle for starting role. Podziemski is in the mix to open the 2024-25 season as the Warriors' starting shooting guard, Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area writes. The Warriors will have Stephen Curry running the show at point guard, but it's unclear who will start the season next to him in the backcourt. Podziemski seems to be leading the race to earn that role, as he started 28 games as a rookie while Klay Thompson was still part of the Warriors last season. The second-year guard offers a more balanced game compared to other options such as Buddy Hield or De'Anthony Melton. Head coach Steve Kerr needs to make a decision based on who will better complement the star floor general.

Option for San Antonio?. The Spurs could be interested in trading for Ingram, Andy Bailey of Bleacher Report speculates. Ingram's future with the Pelicans is uncertain, and the Spurs could be a good trade partner for New Orleans. They would give Ingram the star role he's looking for, and they would have enough money to hand him an extension. Plus, a trio of Ingram, Victor Wembanyama and Chris Paul would be enough to lift the Spurs into playoff contention. However, there would be several hurdles to overcome to make the deal happen, which is why Bailey suggests a three-team trade that also includes the Cavaliers.

Shakes off wrist injury. Miller (wrist) made one appearance for the Hornets in the Las Vegas Summer League, producing 23 points (7-16 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 4-4 FT), eight rebounds and two assists in 33 minutes in a 94-90 win over the Knicks on July 13. Miller missed the final game of his rookie season April 14 due to a right wrist injury, but his offseason training program doesn't seem to have been affected by the issue. Though the Hornets included him on their Summer League roster, Miller dazzled in his lone appearance before the coaching staff determined it had seen enough from the No. 2 overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, who is locked into a prominent role on the wing heading into his second season. Miller averaged 17.3 points on 44 percent shooting from the field and 37.3 percent shooting from distance over 74 games for the Hornets in 2023-24, but even if he raises his efficiency in Year 2, he may not be in store for a substantial uptick in his scoring. LaMelo Ball (ankle) was limited to just 22 games a season ago, but if the star point guard enjoys better health during the 2024-25 campaign, Miller would likely rank as the Hornets' third option behind Ball and Miles Bridges.

Out at least six weeks. Sensabaugh will miss at least six weeks after tearing an extensor tendon in his left middle finger Saturday during the Summer League, Ryan Miller of KSL.com reports. Sensabaugh had three points, two assists and two rebounds for the Jazz before leaving Saturday's game for good. Despite this setback, Sensabaugh is likely to be 100 percent recovered in time for training camp. Heading into his second season, Sensabaugh could be a rotation player for the Jazz right out of the gate.

Bucks not interested in trading him. The Bucks have "zero interest" in trading Lopez before the start of the 2024-25 season, general manager Jon Horst told Eric Nehm of The Athletic on Friday. "First of all, rumors and chatter are what makes the league so interesting and so fun, so people are always going to speculate and talk about it. And I typically don't talk about any of this stuff with the media, but I will say, because Brook is so core to who we are, we have zero intentions of trading Brook," Horst said. Horst went as far as saying that he hopes Lopez retires with Milwaukee, essentially putting down every potential rumor involving the departure of the big man. Lopez has started at least 78 regular-season games in each of the last two campaigns and plays a huge role for the Bucks on the defensive side of the ball, so it makes sense for Milwaukee to try and keep him around.

Potential trade candidate. Brown has been mentioned as one of the players most likely to be traded during the 2024-25 NBA season, according to Kurt Helin of NBC Sports. One of the most versatile wing players in the league, Brown would be an excellent addition to a contender, and the best proof of what he can do lies in the key role he played for the Nuggets in their title-winning season in 2023-24. Brown averaged 10.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 2.9 assists across 27.9 minutes in 67 regular-season appearances in the 2023-24 season while playing for the Pacers and Raptors, and given Toronto's rebuilding situation, expect Brown to be mentioned in trade talks quite often.

Nears triple-double Friday. Cunningham tabulated 25 points (10-16 FG, 1-4 3PT, 4-4 FT), 12 rebounds, nine assists and two steals in 31 minutes during Friday's 109-91 preseason win over Phoenix. After a slow start to his preseason, Cunningham came alive Friday, falling one assist short of a triple-double. It was a dominant performance by Cunningham, reminding fantasy managers just what he is capable of when healthy. Despite an injury-plagued career to this point, Cunningham remains one of the more exciting players in the league. The Pistons have made some savvy moves during the offseason in the hopes of at least being competitive. Managers should cross their fingers that Cunningham can stay on the floor and that Detroit stays relevant beyond February.

Poor shooting in preseason win. Cunningham delivered 13 points (5-13 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists, a steal and a block across 25 minutes in Sunday's 120-87 preseason win over the Bucks. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Reaches five-year extension. Cunningham (knee) and the Pistons agreed on a five-year, $224 million maximum rookie extension Tuesday, Adrian Wojnarowski of ESPN reports. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Chip on shoulder for 2024-25?. Cunningham is mentioned as one of three Pistons who have "something to prove" ahead of the 2024-25 season, according to Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press. Sankofa believes the Pistons should improve compared to their disastrous 2023-24 season, but for that to happen, Cunningham is one of several players who will need to improve and show he's worthy of his role in the team. The pressure on Cunningham will be even bigger this season, as he recently signed a max rookie scale extension in the offseason. The star floor general averaged 22.7 points, 7.5 assists and 4.3 rebounds in 33.5 minutes over 62 regular-season games.

Might remain with Brooklyn. Johnson could be part of the Nets' roster by the time the 2024-25 regular season starts in October, according to NetsDaily.com. Several teams have been linked with Johnson throughout the offseason, and while the Nets have been listening to offers, it seems the wing will stay with the Nets, at least during the opening months of the 2024-25 season. One of the reasons why Johnson is not expected to be traded lies in the fact that Brooklyn's general manager, Sean Marks, might be asking for more than what he's already receiving in trade proposals. That's the same approach Marks is using with the other coveted trade chip in the Nets roster, Dorian Finney-Smith.

Could handle more playmaking duties. Thomas is expected to have increased responsibilities in the playmaking department during the upcoming season, according to C.J. Holmes of The New York Daily News. Thomas and Nic Claxton will be the Nets' most important players during the 2024-25 season, and both will play key roles on offense for new head coach Jordi Fernandez. Based on how Fernandez's previous offenses in Denver and Sacramento operated, both players are expected to have the ball in their hands a lot more, but it's unclear if they'll be comfortable with such responsibility. Thomas averaged a career-high 2.9 assists per game in 2023-24 but also committed 1.9 turnovers per contest.

Could be traded on expiring deal. LeVert could potentially be traded with only one year remaining on his current contract, Ashish Mathur of HoopsWire.com reports. LeVert is coming off a productive season, during which he averaged 14.0 points, 5.1 assists, 4.1 rebounds and 1.6 stocks while shooting 42.1 percent from the field over 68 regular-season games. Despite his decent production, LeVert shot just 32.5 percent from deep and can be a streaky shooter at times. The club may look to obtain a three-and-D forward on a longer contract who could bring solid perimeter shooting and defense to a squad that ranked 19th in threes made last year. The Cavaliers have reportedly expressed interest in Cameron Johnson, an effective three-and-D forward who has shot 39.2 percent from deep throughout his career.

Future international player?. Holmgren could represent Team USA in the 2028 Olympics, according to Joel Lorenzi of The Oklahoman. Holmgren has a strong chance to play for Team USA in the near future, as his skill set translates well to the international game. He's an elite shot-blocker and rim protector who stretches out defenses with his range at the offensive end. Those traits tend to play well at the FIBA level, though for that to happen, he'll have to continue improving. Holmgren averaged 16.5 points, 7.9 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.8 bocks per game during the 2023-24 regular season while starting each of the Thunder's 82 games.

Set for starting role?. Braun is expected to move into the starting lineup in the 2024-25 regular season following the departure of Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, who signed with the Magic, according to Bennett Durando of The Denver Post. While Braun is a different player than Caldwell-Pope, there's a belief he can hold his own and replace KCP on the defensive end, as he's bigger and already considered an above-average defender by league standards. Braun has shot 37.3 percent from three-point range throughout his career, but he needs to improve his corner-three skill in order to effectively replace Caldwell-Pope as a reliable offensive threat.

Undergoes knee procedure. Wood underwent a successful arthroscopic surgical procedure on his left knee Monday, Mike Trudell of Spectrum SportsNet reports. The forward will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, meaning he will miss the start of the 2024-25 season. This is a tough blow for Wood, as it will set him back with his offseason training. Wood exercised his $3.04 million player option in May and was already facing an uphill battle for playing time in the Lakers' crowded frontcourt, and this certainly won't help.

Resting Monday. Paul (rest) has been ruled out for Monday's preseason opener against the Thunder, Paul Garcia of ProjectSpurs.com reports. The 19-year NBA veteran will join Devin Vassell (foot) and Victor Wembanyama (rest) on the bench Monday, allowing the Spurs to take an extended look at Stephon Castle and and Tre Jones. Paul's next chance to play during the preseason will come Wednesday against the Magic.

Relishing big role with Spurs. Paul decided to sign with the Spurs because he'll likely have a bigger role than the one he had with the Warriors in 2023-24, according to Kelly Iko of The Athletic. "The opportunity to play. That was a big part of it," Paul said. "I think for me, especially since signing in San Antonio, a couple things I've been focused on have been making sure I'm ready to play. Totally different role than I was in last season." After starting all 1,214 of his regular season NBA games prior to the 2023-24 campaign, Paul came off the bench in 40 of his 58 appearances for the Warriors and averaged a career-low 26.4 minutes per game. However, Spurs head coach Gregg Popovich envisions a bigger role for the 39-year-old floor general. "I said, 'Be Chris Paul.' I probably won't coach him a lick," Popovich said, per Iko. "I'll just try to infuse what our strategy is, how we play, what we're looking to do. Give him information but he's gonna play and be Chris Paul."

New York tried to acquire him. The Knicks tried to acquire Capela via trade during the offseason, according to Ian Begley of SNY.tv. The Knicks discussed a deal with the Hawks involving Capela this offseason, but these two parties failed to reach an agreement. Don't be surprised if Capela becomes available before the trade deadline, as the Hawks are trending toward rebuilding and Capela will be a free agent next summer. Plus, they could part ways with him and promote Onyeka Okongwu to a starting role.

Will miss Summer League finale. Williams has been ruled out for Sunday's Summer League game against the Pistons due to an illness. The No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, Williams played well in Summer League action but will miss the finale due to a minor ailment. He should be fully healthy for training camp and is expected to compete for a rotational role as a rookie.

Fares well in loss. Williams recorded 14 points (6-11 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks in 31 minutes during Monday's 82-70 Summer League loss to the Kings. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Candidate for regular role. Williams could be in line for a regular role in the Jazz rotation in his rookie year following a strong Summer League display, according to Tony Jones of The Athletic. Jones believes that Williams should get immediate playing time in the NBA and go through the natural ups and downs of a rookie, rather than being sent to the G League. Even though Williams struggled badly in the Salt Lake City Summer League, he thrived in Las Vegas and showed glimpses of the player he might become with regular reps in The Association. The rookie could crack the NBA rotation as a rookie, and Utah's rebuilding process could allow him extra minutes on the floor.

Remains out Thursday. Martin (wrist) didn't play in Thursday's preseason game against the Grizzlies. Martin continues to fight through a sprained wrist, and the injury forced him to miss another exhibition. Look for Tidjane Salaun, Tre Mann and Seth Curry to continue to get more run in the preseason until Martin is cleared for play.

Considered day-to-day. Martin is considered day-to-day and will miss Sunday's preseason opener against the Knicks due to a thumb laceration and sprained right wrist. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.
Cleared to play. Martin (ankle) was able to go through Tuesday's practice to open training camp. Subscribe now to instantly reveal our take on this news.

Joins Orlando on two-year deal. Joseph and the Magic agreed to a two-year contract Wednesday, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports. This could be a strong indication that Orlando has moved on from bringing back Markelle Fultz in free agency. A 13-year NBA veteran, Joseph holds career regular-season averages of 6.9 points, 3.0 assists and 2.5 rebounds, but it's unlikely he'll play a big role in Orlando with the likes of Jalen Suggs, Cole Anthony and Anthony Black in the backcourt.

Interest growing on trade market. Several teams including the Raptors and Nets could be open to trading for Russell, Ashish Mathur of HoopsWire.com reports. Russell could be headed out of Los Angeles after spending the entirety of the 2023-24 season there, during which he averaged 18.0 points, 6.3 assists, 3.1 rebounds and 0.9 steals across 32.7 minutes per game over 76 regular-season contests. While both the Nets and Raptors are in a transitional period, adding Russell to the books could provide some mentorship for the squad's younger players, as both clubs are in the process of rebuilding. The 28-year-old opted into his player option for the upcoming season, and he has expressed his desire to stay in Los Angeles. However, if the Lakers do decide to trade him there is a market, and he could be a decent option for any team looking to add short-term money to the books. Moreover, the Lakers have expressed interest in Cameron Johnson and Dorian Finney-Smith, so the Nets could potentially be a realistic landing spot.

Sitting out SL finale. Knecht won't play in Saturday's Summer League game against the Bulls for rest purposes, Mike Trudell of Spectrum SportsNet reports. The Lakers are opting to rest Knecht, Bronny James and Maxwell Lewis for Friday's Summer League finale. After starting slowly in the California Classic, Knecht has showcased the three-level scoring ability that he used to dominate at Tennessee last season.

Logs 28 minutes Sunday. Fox recorded 11 points (5-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt), seven rebounds, three assists and three steals across 28 minutes in Sunday's 108-85 preseason loss to the Trail Blazers. The Kings played their projected starters between 28 and 30 minutes, and even though Sacramento looked overmatched at times, there shouldn't be any notable changes in the rotation, let alone the starting unit before the regular-season opener against the Timberwolves on Oct. 24. Fox had one of the best years of his career in 2023-24, averaging career-high marks in several categories including points (26.6), rebounds (4.6) and steals (2.0) per game.

Sustains serious wrist injury. Exum has sustained a right wrist injury that could require surgery, Shams Charania of The Athletic reports. Treatment options are being evaluated for Exum, though he could miss a significant amount of time due to the injury. The 29-year-old typically served as a spark off the bench last season, during which he averaged 7.8 points, 2.9 assists and 2.7 rebounds across 19.8 minutes per game in 55 regular-season appearances (17 starts). Exum will presumably miss serious time, and if he does Naji Marshall, Jaden Hardy and Quentim Grimes are candidates for extra minutes.

Practices fully for Australia. Extension not happening soon. Bridges is not expected to sign a contract extension with the Knicks before the start of the 2024-25 season, according to Bobby Marks of ESPN. The 26-year-old averaged 21.0 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 0.9 steals over 69 regular-season appearances in 2023-24.

To miss start of season. Robinson (ankle) will not be ready for the beginning of the NBA season, Ian Begley of SportsNet New York reports. With Robinson sidelined to begin the season, Julius Randle could spend plenty of time at center in smaller lineups, while Precious Achiuwa and Jericho Sims will have more opportunities to earn meaningful minutes.

Claxton averaged a career-high 2.1 assists per game in 2023-24.

Knicks might show interest. The Knicks could look at Williams if they were to upgrade their depth at the center position for the 2024-25 season, according to John Hollinger and Fred Katz of The Athletic. As things stand now, the Knicks are set to open the season with Mitchell Robinson as their starting center, while Precious Achiuwa and Jericho Sims are the potential backups. That's an area where the Knicks could use an upgrade. While they're not likely to add another center before the start of the campaign, adding another big man as the season progresses could quickly become a priority. Considering Williams could end up being the third-string center at Portland behind Deandre Ayton and Donovan Clingan, he could be had for a reasonably decent haul. Williams would solidify the team's depth down low.
